title: Universal Approximation Theorems for Dynamical Systems with Infinite-Time Horizon Guarantees
claim: Different classes of dynamical systems nest inside one another, and our guarantees extend beyond the narrow fading-memory class to multistable, oscillatory and continuous-attractor systems.
layout: Single panel of nested rounded boxes, innermost to outermost, rotated side labels
description: A single Venn-style diagram of nested rounded rectangles that share the lower-left corner. The innermost grey box says 'fading memory system'. Around it is a blue box labeled F_FP, 'multi-stability'. Next is a mint-green box labeled F_LC, 'oscillations'. The outermost is a red/pink box labeled F_CA, 'marginally stable manifolds'. Two rotated labels sit on the right edge. The green strip reads 'hyperbolic (structurally stable)'. The red strip reads 'non-hyperbolic'. The labels are large black sans-serif text with calligraphic math symbols at upper left. The eye goes first to the colorful nested layers and then to the small grey fading-memory core. The figure shows how the system classes fit together and which ones the theory covers.
caption: The landscape of universal approximation for dynamical systems. Existing infinite-time results require the fading memory property (FMP), excluding multistability; FMP systems with a hyperbolic equilibrium lie in $\mcF_{\mathrm{FP}}$. We prove Neural ODEs are dense in Morse-Smale systems ($\mcF_{\mathrm{FP}}$, $\mcF_{\mathrm{LC}}$) and normally hyperbolic continuous attractors ($\mcF_{\mathrm{CA}}$), subject to isochrony for oscillatory manifolds.
abstract: Universal approximation theorems establish the expressive capacity of neural network architectures. A trained dynamical model can pass every finite-time test yet fail in the long run in three ways: it can settle to the wrong steady state, drift out of phase, or collapse a continuum of memory states into isolated ones. We consider models whose vector field is parameterized expressively enough to approximate any target vector field together with its Jacobian, e.g., Neural ODEs. We prove that such models can avoid all three failures, matching a target system's trajectories over the infinite-time horizon $[0,\infty)$ on all but a small set of initial conditions ($\varepsilon$-$Î´$ closeness: trajectory error within $\varepsilon$ except for initial conditions of measure $< Î´$). We cover three target classes, the dynamical primitives of decision-making, rhythm generation, and analog memory: structurally stable systems with a finite number of hyperbolic periodic orbits (fixed points or limit cycles via exact period matching), and continuous attractors that are normally hyperbolic manifolds of fixed points or of isochronous limit cycles (via discretization). A temporal generalization bound, $\varepsilon$-$Î´$ closeness implies time-averaged $L^p$ error $\leq \varepsilon^p + Î´\cdot D^p$ for all $t \geq 0$, connects these guarantees to training metrics. This is the first universal approximation framework for multistable dynamics over an unbounded horizon.
